prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map reveals a downward-angled tabletop workspace extending from roughly 0.3–0.5 metres in the lower foreground to about 1.2–1.8 metres in the upper background, where the camera wearer sits below the frame with two to three other people seated around the table about 0.8–1.5 metres away from the wearer and 0.5–1.0 metres from one another. Bright foreground silhouettes (0.3–0.7 metres) show the camera wearer's outstretched arms and a large white sack on the right within immediate arm's reach, while medium-grey regions (0.7–1.2 metres) mark clusters of small white bags, green-and-white packets on the table, and neighboring people's hands reaching in from the upper right and upper left. Across frames 1 to 3, the camera pitches downward and turns slightly left toward the central pile of bags before panning right and tilting slightly up in frames 4 and 5, causing the large right-side sack to retreat out of view in frames 2–3 and reappear close in the lower right at 0.3–0.5 metres in frames 4–5. Compared to the motion-blurred RGB strip, the depth map more clearly separates the elevation and 3D layering of the tall open sack rim, overlapping forearms, and stacked packets above the flat table plane, though all people's heads remain cropped out of view so gaze toward the wearer cannot be determined. However, depth estimates look unreliable inside the open mouth of the white sack in frame 1 (where the recessed interior is rendered overly bright) and in the upper corners where table surfaces and distant bags drop off into flat black voids.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map fails to capture almost the entire scene layout, detecting masks only in frames 1 and 4 while leaving frames 2, 3, and 5 completely blank despite the table, bags, and multiple people remaining visible within 0.3–1.8 metres in the RGB strip. In frame 1, it identifies a 'person' mask for the camera wearer's lower-left forearm and knee at 0.3–0.6 metres, a second 'person' mask at the top center for a seated individual about 1.0–1.5 metres away facing toward the table center (head cropped out, not looking at the wearer), and a small 'cup' mask at 0.8 metres on the left that actually corresponds to a small white pouch within arm's reach. In frame 4, a single large 'person' mask on the right fuses the camera wearer's lower-right arm (0.4 metres), an adjacent person's reaching arms (0.8–1.2 metres), and the large foreground white sack into one fragmented silhouette. While the frame 1 masks help isolate the boundary between the camera wearer's reaching left limb and the background seated person's legs across the table, the map is highly unreliable due to severe false negatives across all five frames, misclassifying a white bag as a cup, and merging distinct foreground objects and people in frame 4.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is almost entirely empty across the five-frame sequence, detecting only a single magenta right-hand skeleton in the lower-left center of frame 2 and failing to render any yellow body skeletons or other hands in frames 1, 3, 4, and 5. In frame 2, this detected hand belongs to the camera wearer's outstretched right arm at roughly 0.5–0.7 metres in front of the torso, positioned just above the tabletop and within immediate reach of a white plastic bag and adjacent small pouches about 0.1–0.3 metres to its right. From the RGB context, the camera wearer's body is below the bottom edge facing forward toward the table while other participants sit 0.8–1.5 metres away to the upper left and right with their torsos and heads occluded or outside the field of view, preventing any visibility of eye contact. Although the single hand skeleton in frame 2 precisely localizes the wearer's curled fingers and wrist orientation during heavy RGB motion blur as the arm reaches forward, the map provides no tracking of how the wearer's or others' limbs approach, retreat, or turn across the remaining frames and is therefore largely unreliable for multi-person spatial understanding.
